# N5: Review notes, data-ids

A check of the Spreadsheets module ([its section](../README.md#journeys-and-checks)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/notes/5-data-ids.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured, and a limit its words don’t give is added after it, in the script’s test (“its test: …”).

## What it checks

Lane's review notes (5 Nov), data-ids. TABLE-LAYOUTS: in the data tables, columns move (drag a heading; Columns' up and down on touch) and change width (drag a heading's edge; arrow keys), the layout is remembered and saves as a named view that reopens, and the table exports (CSV, .xlsx) exactly as shown. READABLE-IDS: every goal has a key G-n, unique, shown on the goal, in the Goals table and the data tables; /goals/G-n opens the goal. The AI assistant's side (find_goals, get_goal and every tool taking a goal accept a key) is checked in evals/data-ids.eval.ts, which needs no browser.

## Where it looks

- 1280 × 800, as grace, at `/data`
- 390 × 844, as rhea, at `/data`, on a touch screen
- 768 × 1000, as mateo, at `/goals?scope=all&view=table`
- 1024 × 1000, as mateo, at `/goals?scope=all&view=table`
- 1440 × 900, as amara, at `/goals/G-17`

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day. {…} is a value the script works out as it runs.
